answer: Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the thread reward in the inlet ledger costs the operator directly, and the nadir audit records each payout. A farm of 260 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 24% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the attacker's own capital. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
